decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY selecting Option B and recording the reach, terminal-softening, and cross-glyph refinement variants.
The client explicitly requires the Hero V reach study to be carried through the second V while preserving its slope and geometry, and no same-message candidate Event exists.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

This rendering made me feel really excited. We are getting so incredibly close! Beautiful work, Abdulbari—truly.

After sitting with them for a while, I think Option B is the strongest direction. It has the confidence, restraint, and architectural quality I was hoping for.

Option A feels a little too sharp to me, while Option C has a softness that I like, but I think Option B captures the overall character best.

For the next round, I'd love to explore just a few very subtle refinements while keeping everything else exactly as it is:

1\. Start with Option B and extend the right arm of the Hero V ever so slightly—just a touch more reach while maintaining the exact same slope and geometry. Please carry that same refinement through the second V and the É accent. This should be an extremely subtle change. It might actually be helpful to include a horizontal reference line so I can clearly see how much higher the right arm extends above the left arm. I think this difference will ultimately become one of the defining characteristics shared by the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

2\. Starting from that same version of Option B, keep the identical amount of reach, but soften the terminal ever so slightly. I'm not looking for more curvature—just a gentler finish while preserving the same architectural character. Perhaps the corners become just a touch softer, but the tip itself remains straight rather than curving.

3\. Take Option C and give it that same subtle increase in reach, again keeping the slope and overall geometry unchanged, and apply it consistently to the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

At this point, I think we're working in very small refinements. I'd like to keep the overall architecture locked and simply explore these final nuances.

Thank you again—I’m so excited to see the result!

value_updates.right_arm_reach_study: extend the second V right arm extremely slightly while preserving its slope and overall geometry

decisions.reason: The source changes shared terminal reach but does not change the requirement that the Hero V and É accent highest points align; applying the refinement consistently preserves that rule.
The É accent remains a literal geometric derivative of the Hero V terminal; the shared reach and terminal studies do not alter the existing one-to-one derivation rule.
The source concerns glyph reach and terminal geometry and does not change the selected Satin Reflection finish or champagne-gold distribution.
The client limits the requested refinements to the Hero V, second V, and É accent and asks to keep everything else unchanged, so the E and L requirements remain unchanged.
The subtle reach study affects second-V glyph geometry, but it preserves the existing qualitative hierarchy in which only its right arm extends slightly above the E and L.
The source retains Option B and asks that everything apart from the listed terminal nuances remain unchanged, so the selected Balanced Flow kerning remains valid.
The source does not change the E or L scale or their alignment to the second V's left arm.
Extending the glyphs' right arms while preserving their slope and overall geometry does not change the common alignment of their bottom points.
The source provides design feedback but does not change the obligation to include rationale with review rounds.
